parsed.explanation: No criminal statute applies to trans visitors (repealed 2004, dead-letter even before), no documented police targeting, facility bans, custody practices, or border exposures, and documented civil-society freedom (Prides since 2013, freely registering organisations) plus a protective external posture. Against this: no legal gender recognition with a documented refusal of even a name change, no gender-identity anti-discrimination protection, and the only trans-specific harms are one activist's undated verbal abuse and two physical attacks, alongside a finding of continuing societal discrimination. Thin-data extrapolation from decriminalisation, no enforcement record, and tolerant regional standing resolves above midpoint; absent documented protections or traveller-facing positives, it stays in Reduced Risk's lower half, not higher. Unknowns (border screening, facilities, custody) are open questions, not exposures.

entry_documents.interaction: No LGR framework and a documented refusal of a legal name change mean no local precedent for documentary flexibility if a passport marker mismatch is raised; but no border or marker-check practice is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented arrests, raids, or custody placement rules touching trans people; criminalisation repealed 2004 with no enforcement record either way.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No statute or practice on bathrooms, wards, or segregated spaces appears in the dossier; nothing supports either exclusion or inclusion.

care_services.interaction: No evidence on HRT import, refill, or emergency-care treatment of trans visitors in either direction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2010 foreign human-rights report: societal discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity persists despite legal protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Labour code bans sexual-orientation discrimination since 2008 (not gender identity); strong UN-level protective foreign posture incl. 2025 regional trans-inclusive declaration.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Anti-discrimination machinery exists but excludes gender identity, leaving a trans visitor with thin formal recourse.

minors_guardians.interaction: Dossier contains nothing age-dependent; no traveller-facing rule distinguishes minors or guardians.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One activist reported verbal violence and two physical attacks (undated, pre-2016); no later instance documented; no rate can be stated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Functioning civil society; country characterised as markedly free for LGBT people regionally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is undocumented; hate-crime recourse untested.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity discrimination protection; no legal-recognition route; tolerance polling measures only homosexual neighbours, not trans acceptance.
remedies_unknowns.protection: LGBTIQ organisations register freely; Prides since 2013; 2024 UPR anti-discrimination commitments.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions — border screening, facilities, custody, care — are unresolved rather than documented exposures; thin-data silence is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Marisol Union documents a universal-exposure ward-assignment rule by document sex; this dossier documents no traveller-facing rule at all. Above 0.55-C on severity, though this jurisdiction lacks documented working remedies that 0.55-C partially has.

Caldera at 0.75 has trained border officers, functioning appeal tribunals, and low-moderate severity with documented remedy paths. This dossier documents no border practice and no working remedy for trans-specific harms — the activist's blocked name change shows no relief — so it sits below.

Drellia at 0.45 imposes universal registration and database disclosure creating durable outing exposure. This jurisdiction documents no registration, surveillance, or disclosure mechanism; its harms are thinner (societal discrimination, two undated attacks), placing it clearly above.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of decriminalisation without documented enforcement against trans people, embedded civil-society freedom, and a state with a protective external LGBTI posture — but no internal protections reaching trans visitors: no legal gender recognition (with a documented refusal even of a name change), no gender-identity anti-discrimination ground, and one documented pattern of societal violence against a trans person (undated, thin). The documented tolerance findings are LGB-framed and cannot be read as trans acceptance, and 2026 source recency does not establish current enforcement practice. No traveller-facing exposure is documented on any axis, but absence of evidence is not safety in a thin dossier; structural signals (repealed statute, no relief precedent, functioning but gender-identity-blind institutions) resolve the score moderately above the midpoint, at the lower edge of Reduced Risk.
